Definition: Expressions of confidence or demonstrations of a student's technical, critical, communication, or academic competencies.
Example: communication skill, academic writing ability, quality of final arguments structure

Definition: Concerns that raw data could lead to misinterpretation, false assupmtions, or incorrect conclusions by assessors.
Example: I would rather not share this with teacher as this could create biases

Definition: Rationales focused on demonstrating authentic individual effort, authorship, and ownership of the work.
Example: Teachers can assess my work and know how much work is done by me

Definition: Exposing personal struggles, mistakes, low proficiency, or hesitations during the learning process.
Example: it reveals full writing process and mistakes

Definition: Data required solely because it forms part of the final deliverable.
Example: It's the finalised form of the assessment

Definition: Rationales focused on utilising data to drive learning growth, refine skills, enhance future performance, or guide pedagogical support
Example: Teachers can help me identify areas of improvement.

Definition: Rationales focused on exposing the student's cognitive workflow, research strategy, and problem-solving approach.
Example: it might show ur developement throughout the process

Definition: Concerns regarding social comparison, judgemenet, or perceived inadequacy when student data or metrics are exposed to classmates.
Example: Not every student can finish a report in the same time

Definition: Concerns regarding unauthorised copying, intellectual property theft, or uncredited use of work by peers.
Example: keep privacy from other student to not copy

Definition: Feelings of anxiety or discomfort from being observed, monitored, or evaluated by authoritative figures.
Example: I don't want any pressure of someone checking

Definition: Concerns regarding personal boundaries, surveillance anxiety, or unauthroised exposure of personal information.
Example: Would not share with anyone as could be considered personal data

Definition: Rationales focused on using evidence to defend against academic integrity allegations, prove genuine authorship, or safeguard against false claims
Example: Needed in the case of plagiarism cases

Definition: Data perceived as unnecessary, noisy, or having low value for evaluating the task.
Example: I don't think it'd be so important for teachers

Definition: Rationales that place conditions on data sharing based on boundaries, platform restrictions, or the level of detail/aggregation.
Example: Should be fine if it's on a confined platform
